body: Can also confirm this in 4.3.stable and 4.2.2.stable
I think it's likely that this is the same issue as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105074

> I think it's likely that this is the same issue as [#105074](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/105074)

I'm not sure, 4.3 and 4.2 didn't have Betsy (and it only runs in the editor anyway)
RenderingServerDefault uses the same construct, so it doesn't have to Betsy that is causing a conflict (but yes it could be something else)

> RenderingServerDefault uses the same construct, so it doesn't have to Betsy that is causing a conflict (but yes it could be something else)

Looks like we don't have any other pump tasks enabled (PhysicsServer2D, RenderingServer, or Betsy). When running through the editor I get a crash. ~But running in the debugger I can see were are indeed deadlocked when trying to sync the PhysicsServer~

Looks like a nullptr exception here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a8598cd8e261716fa3addb6f10bb57c03a061be9/scene/3d/physics/soft_body_3d.cpp#L85-L88

Seems to be a bug with the RenderingServerHandler. Likely somewhere is assuming that Physics and Rendering run on the main thread. From what I can see SoftBody3D owns the RenderingServerHandler but the Physics Server interacts with it heavily despite being on a different thread. 

_edit: Actually the issue is very obvious now_

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a8598cd8e261716fa3addb6f10bb57c03a061be9/scene/3d/physics/soft_body_3d.cpp#L441-L443

`open`sets the `write_buffer` to a valid pointer. `close` sets it to a `nullptr`. This code only works if the PhysicsServer is on the same thread as the SoftBody

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a8598cd8e261716fa3addb6f10bb57c03a061be9/scene/3d/physics/soft_body_3d.cpp#L73-L79

I think my proposal at godotengine/godot-proposals#12670 is needed to fix this.

There are (at least) 2 problems:

The first is that `PhysicsServer3D::soft_body_update_rendering_server()` does not invoke the rendering handler before it returns, it invokes it at some arbitrary point in the future on the physics thread, which the SoftBody3D code does not expect.  My proposal includes replacing this API with a `soft_body_set_state_sync_callback()` instead.  (I have some work in progress code that is nearly complete to implement this part of the proposal.)

The second problem is that `PhysicsServer3D::soft_body_set_mesh()` can cause a deadlock, because this attempts to access the RenderingServer from the physics thread.  This causes things to get stuck as follows:

* On the main thread, `Main::iteration()` calls `PhysicsServer3D::get_singleton()->sync()`, which waits for the physics thread to flush and process everything in its command queue.
* On the physics thread, if it has a `soft_body_set_mesh()` call to process in the command queue, this needs to call `RenderingServer::mesh_surface_get_arrays()` to get the mesh data.  However, this function has to run on the main thread, which can't process the command since it is stuck waiting on the physics server.

The `PhysicsServer3D::soft_body_set_settings()` part of my proposal would fix this deadlock.  (The experimental code to run the rendering server on a separate thread would also address this problem, but it seems like we potentially would still need to think carefully about the dependency hierarchy, and which servers are allowed to block on other servers.)
